items.hook: The best books to read in July: new paperbacks from Andrew O’Hagan, Miriam Toews and Oyinkan Braithwaite
items.body:
Looking for a new reading recommendation? Here are some fantastic new paperbacks, from the gripping story of an international murder case to a state-of-the-nation yarn

***

items.hook: The Soviet Union's robotic probe Luna 24 successfully lands on the Moon.
items.body: The Soviet Union, officially the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics (USSR), was a transcontinental country that spanned much of Eurasia from its formation in 1922 until its dissolution in 1991. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: A Great Fire in Thessaloniki, Greece, destroys 32% of the city leaving 70,000 individuals homeless.
items.body: The Great Thessaloniki Fire of 1917 destroyed two thirds of the city of Thessaloniki, the second-largest city in Greece, leaving more than 70,000 homeless. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Princess Abe accedes to the imperial Japanese throne as Empress Genmei.
items.body: Year 707 (DCCVII) was a common year starting on Saturday of the Julian calendar. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Civil rights movement: James Meredith becomes the first African American to graduate from the University of Mississippi.
items.body: The civil rights movement was a social movement in the United States from 1954 to 1968 which aimed to abolish legalized racial segregation, discrimination, and disenfranchisement in the country, which most commonly affected African Americans. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Following the surrender of Baghdad, Seljuk Sultan Mas'ud replaces Abbasid caliph Al-Rashid Billah with his uncle Al-Muqtafi.
items.body: The Siege of Baghdad was a fifty-day blockade of Baghdad, the seat of the Abbasid caliphs, in 1136. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: The Hole is a 2001 British psychological thriller film directed by Nick Hamm, based on the 1993 novel After the Hole by Guy Burt.
items.body: The film stars Thora Birch, Desmond Harrington, Daniel Brocklebank, Laurence Fox, Keira Knightley, and Embeth Davidtz. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Space Opera is a 2018 science fiction novel by Catherynne M.
items.body: Valente, about a galactic version of the Eurovision Song Contest. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Earl Spencer to 'tell the truth' about his sister Princess Diana in new book
items.body: Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is due to be released in the UK next month, nearly 30 years after she died.

items.hook: The 100 best novels of all time
items.body: The top 100 novels of all time published in English, as voted for by authors, critics and academics worldwide. How many have you read?

items.hook: Shōnen is a Japanese novel by Yasunari Kawabata.
items.body: It was first published in a serialized form between 1948 and 1949 and later as a book in 1952. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: For Us, the Living: A Comedy of Customs is a science fiction novel by American writer Robert A.
items.body: It was written in 1938 and published for the first time in 2003. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: The Huguenot King Henry III of Navarre marries the Catholic Margaret of Valois, ostensibly to reconcile the feuding Protestants and Catholics of France.
items.body: The Huguenots are a religious group of French Protestants who held to the Reformed (Calvinist) tradition of Protestantism. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.body: Mandamai Forest Reserve is a protected forest reserve in Pitas District of Kudat Division in Sabah, Malaysia. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Trapped is a science fiction novel written by the Canadian author James Alan Gardner and published in 2002 by HarperCollins Publishers under its various imprints.
items.body: The book is the sixth installment in Gardner's "League of Peoples" series of novels, set in the mid-25th century. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Actress Phyllida Law, mother of Emma and Sophie Thompson, dies at 94
items.body: Law appeared in films alongside both of her daughters, Dame Emma and Sophie, including 1996's Emma.
